text.title: Spring Boot Patterns Failure Modes
text.summary: 8 antipatterns observed in real Spring Boot 3 codebases. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Controller method 200 lines long, computing business rules, formatting dates, hashing passwords.
antipattern.root-cause: Author skipped the service layer "for speed".
antipattern.fix: Move logic into `@Service`; controller stays thin (validate, delegate, return DTO). Enforce a line-of-code budget in CI.

antipattern.symptom: Endpoint leaks `passwordHash`, `deletedAt`, lazy proxy artefacts in the JSON response.
antipattern.root-cause: Same class used as JPA entity and API DTO.
antipattern.fix: Define a Java record DTO; map via MapStruct inside the service. Add a feature test asserting response keys match the expected set.

antipattern.symptom: Some endpoints return `{"error": "..."}`, others `{"message": "..."}`, others 500 with a raw stack trace.
antipattern.root-cause: No `@RestControllerAdvice`; each controller invents its own shape.
antipattern.fix: Add one `@RestControllerAdvice` mapping every domain exception to RFC 7807 `ProblemDetail`.

antipattern.symptom: List endpoint executes 200 SQL queries for 200 results; profile shows one query per row.
antipattern.root-cause: Controller iterates entities and touches lazy associations after the transaction closes.
antipattern.fix: Move iteration inside the service `@Transactional` boundary and use `JOIN FETCH` / `@EntityGraph`. Map to DTO inside the transaction.

antipattern.symptom: Unit test cannot instantiate the bean without booting Spring; refactor that changes the constructor breaks tests.
antipattern.fix: Switch to constructor injection; declare fields `private final`. Add a static-analysis rule (`ArchUnit`) banning `@Autowired` on fields.

antipattern.symptom: `LazyInitializationException` thrown while Jackson serialises the response. The same code path passes in tests, where a transaction is still open, and fails at runtime.
antipattern.root-cause: An entity crossed the service boundary and its lazy associations were touched after the Hibernate session closed.
antipattern.fix: Convert the entity to a DTO inside the service while `@Transactional` is still active, and declare the associations the DTO needs with `@EntityGraph` or `JOIN FETCH` on the repository method.

antipattern.symptom: A malformed payload reaches the service and fails deep in business logic as a `NullPointerException` or a constraint violation from the database; the client gets a 500 instead of a 400.
antipattern.root-cause: `@Valid` missing on the controller parameter, or the request record carries no validation annotations, so nothing rejects the payload at the boundary.
antipattern.fix: Annotate the parameter `@Valid` and the record fields with Bean Validation constraints per `validation-on-controller`; let the `@RestControllerAdvice` map `MethodArgumentNotValidException` to a `ProblemDetail` 400.

antipattern.symptom: `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*` in `application.yml`. `/actuator/env` returns datasource passwords and `/actuator/heapdump` downloads process memory to anyone who can reach the port.
antipattern.root-cause: Wildcard exposure was set to make a probe work, and the security config was never narrowed afterwards.
antipattern.fix: Replace the wildcard with an explicit list (`health,info,prometheus`), put the actuator behind Spring Security, and expose only liveness/readiness health groups unauthenticated.
